newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART TEST 100 PERCENT RECORD AGAINST CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART TEST 100 PERCENT RECORD AGAINST CHAMPIONS.

text.p: The German Bundesliga's team of the moment, VfB Stuttgart, travel to champions Borussia Dortmund on Saturday to test a beguiling run of form which has brought them four wins and 14 goals in four games.

While Dortmund did little for their confidence but much for their injury list in a dogged midweek European Champions' League win, 1991 champions Stuttgart are fresh, injury-free and ready to turn on the style again.

Much of that is the work of 36-year-old stand-in trainer Joachim Loew, told by club president Gerhard Mayer-Vorfelder that he may get to keep the job if he can continue his run for the next two matches.
Loew was making light of the pressure on the eve of his biggest test so far against a Dortmund side who have won five matches in a row despite failing to shine.
"There's nothing better than travelling to a top-of-the-table game. No team is unbeatable," he said.
Most importantly, Loew has his multinational striking trio of Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov, Brazilian Giovane Elber and German international Fredi Bobic free of injury and firing on all cylinders.
Dortmund, meanwhile, have only 15 fit players in a squad of 27 and heard on Thursday that striker Karlheinz Riedle could be out for months with a slipped disc on his neck.
On the bright side is the form of Heiko Herrlich, who pounced on two defensive blunders to give Dortmund a fortunate 2-1 win against Poland's Widzew Lodz on Wednesday.
But Herrlich is not yet fully match fit since returning from a six-month absence with torn ankle ligaments.
Defender Julio Cesar is doubtful after taking a knock on his knee in the match, and Scottish midfielder Paul Lambert is out, also with a knee injury.

Bayern Munich also have to put their midweek exertions behind them, but in their case it is the psychological shock of a 3-0 first leg drubbing at Valencia which threatens to end their UEFA Cup defence at the first hurdle.

Munich travel to Gelsenkirchen -- just 20 miles (35 km) from Dortmund -- to meet a Schalke side who have their tails up after convincingly beating Roda JC Kerkrade 2-0 on Tuesday in their first European outing for 19 years.

Munich are unbeaten in the league and head the table, having played one game more than Stuttgart. But like Dortmund, they have yet to display any championship style, and simply fell apart against Valencia.
On Saturday they will be without defender Thomas Helmer, who may be out for weeks with a knee sprain, and errant midfield genius Mario Basler, not yet recovered from ligament problems.
"You are the Bundesliga leaders," trainer Giovanni Trapattoni told his expensive stars. "When you are in Schalke, play like it. You've got a few things to make up for."
